The entire selected file is retained; the approximately 96.5-second junction is a listening marker, not a clip boundary. Individual score readings and cuts within each work have not been audited.

Victor is the issuing company in DAHR; the selected Archive item gives the Victrola imprint.

[3] [1]
Catalogue
64989 Documented

Issue number of the 10-inch 78 rpm disc; this is not the matrix number.

[3] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
B-23953, take 2; both études on one side Documented

DAHR identifies Op. 10 No. 5 followed by Op. 25 No. 9; Archive’s matrix_number field repeats issue number 64989, so DAHR supplies the actual matrix.

[3]
Transfer
George Blood, L.P.; Chris Guest (transfer); Kevin Coupe (cleaning) Documented

Archive metadata names the scanning centre and the transferred/cleaned personnel; these are digital-transfer credits, not 1920 session engineers.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer or mastering date is established; upload dates are not used as recording dates.

Processing
78 rpm transfer; flat and equalised versions documented, with 250 Hz turnover for the equalised versions Documented

Archive describes 3.5 mil truncated elliptical and 2.3 mil truncated conical styli. The selected generic MP3 is the provided listening derivative; the exact stylus/equalisation choice for that file is not established.

[1]
Composition rights
Public domain Documented

Chopin died in 1849; this nineteenth-century composition is out of copyright in the programme jurisdictions. This does not determine the recording rights.

[2]
Recording rights
Public domain in the United States: published in 1920 Documented

DAHR’s issue record, MARC 264 field, dates Victor 64989’s publication to 1920 independently of the session date. The selected Archive item also gives 1920. This meets the programme’s published-on-or-before-1925 sound-recording rule; no non-commercial restriction appears in the Archive metadata.

[4] [3] [1]

Alfred Cortot, piano; Victor 64989, matrix B-23953 take 2 (1920). Transfer via George Blood, L.P. and the Internet Archive Great 78 Project; Chris Guest, transfer; Kevin Coupe, cleaning. Historical recording public domain in the United States.
